mcqs.question: Which statement best defines "recording results honestly" in a scientific investigation?

options.A: Writing down only the results that support your hypothesis
options.B: Changing numbers after the experiment to make them look better
options.C: Writing exactly what you observed, even if it does not support your idea
options.D: Guessing the results before the experiment begins

mcqs.answer: Writing exactly what you observed, even if it does not support your idea
mcqs.explanation: Honest recording means noting the actual observations and measurements without altering them to fit any expectation. Option C describes this. Options A and B involve bias or falsification, and D is not recording at all.

mcqs.question: A student measures the height of plants that received fertilizer and those that did not. The data show the fertilized plants grew an average of 3 cm taller. Which sentence correctly uses these results as evidence?

options.A: The fertilizer must be the only reason the plants grew taller because the data prove it
options.B: The plants that received fertilizer grew taller, suggesting the fertilizer may help growth
options.C: The taller plants prove that all fertilizers work for every plant species
options.D: The experiment was unnecessary because the plants grew anyway

mcqs.answer: The plants that received fertilizer grew taller, suggesting the fertilizer may help growth
mcqs.explanation: Using results as evidence means linking observations to a reasonable conclusion while acknowledging they are part of the evidence. Option B does this. Option A overstates certainty, C overgeneralises, and D ignores the evidence.

mcqs.question: In an investigation of how sunlight affects seed germination, the student only used one type of seed and conducted the experiment in a single classroom. Which of the following statements correctly identifies a limitation of this investigation?

options.A: The results cannot be applied to other types of seeds or different environments
options.B: The investigation proved that sunlight is the only factor influencing germination
options.C: Using one classroom makes the experiment faster and more accurate
options.D: The limitation is that the student did not record the temperature

mcqs.answer: The results cannot be applied to other types of seeds or different environments
mcqs.explanation: A limitation is a factor that restricts how widely the findings can be applied. Because only one seed type and one setting were used, the results may not hold for other seeds or locations. Options B and C are inaccurate statements, and D mentions a possible error but not the main limitation described.

mcqs.question: Riya wants to find out whether adding a pinch of salt to water changes how quickly a sugar cube dissolves. What is the primary purpose of her investigation?

options.A: To prove that salt always speeds up dissolution
options.B: To explore how a specific factor (salt) influences the rate of dissolution
options.C: To measure the exact temperature of the water
options.D: To compare different types of sugar cubes

mcqs.answer: To explore how a specific factor (salt) influences the rate of dissolution
mcqs.explanation: The purpose of a scientific investigation is to examine the effect of a chosen variable—in this case, salt—on an outcome, the dissolution rate. Option B states this clearly. Option A assumes a result, C is unrelated, and D shifts focus to a different variable.

mcqs.learning_point: Changing one relevant factor at a time where appropriate
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about changing variables in an experiment?

options.A: Only one relevant factor should be changed at a time to see its effect clearly
options.B: You can change several factors together if you think they all affect the result
options.C: Keeping other factors the same helps you know which factor caused the change
options.D: Changing one factor at a time makes the investigation fair

mcqs.answer: You can change several factors together if you think they all affect the result
mcqs.explanation: The correct scientific practice is to change only one relevant factor at a time. Option B suggests changing many factors simultaneously, which is a misconception. Options A, C, and D correctly describe the proper method.

mcqs.question: Why is it important to keep other relevant conditions the same when investigating the effect of one variable?

options.A: It ensures that any observed change is likely due to the variable being tested
options.B: It makes the experiment look more complicated and impressive
options.C: It allows you to change many things at once without noticing
options.D: It guarantees that the hypothesis will be proven right

mcqs.answer: It ensures that any observed change is likely due to the variable being tested
mcqs.explanation: Controlling other conditions isolates the effect of the variable under study, so any difference in results can be attributed to that variable. Options B, C, and D are incorrect or misleading statements.

mcqs.question: Which pair of investigations best demonstrates the principle of making repeated observations?

options.A: Observing a plant once in the morning and once in the evening
options.B: Measuring the temperature of a room every hour for a whole day
options.C: Testing a single piece of metal for magnetism only once
options.D: Looking at a star through a telescope on a single night

mcqs.answer: Measuring the temperature of a room every hour for a whole day
mcqs.explanation: Repeated observations involve collecting data multiple times under the same conditions to see patterns or changes. Option B does this systematically. Options A only gives two observations at different times, C and D are single observations.

mcqs.question: During a science fair, a student records the height of a plant as 12 cm, even though the ruler actually shows 10 cm, to match the expected outcome. Which action most directly violates the principle of recording results honestly?

options.A: Writing the measurement as 10 cm, the exact value shown on the ruler
options.B: Noting the date and time of each measurement
options.C: Changing the recorded height from 10 cm to 12 cm to fit the hypothesis
options.D: Repeating the measurement three times and taking the average

mcqs.answer: Changing the recorded height from 10 cm to 12 cm to fit the hypothesis
mcqs.explanation: Altering data to fit a hypothesis is dishonest recording. Option C describes this violation. Options A, B, and D are consistent with honest, accurate scientific practice.
